sections.h2: What speed can a North Miami Beach seller expect?
sections.html:
Speed depends on three things: who the buyer is, how they pay, and what the title search finds. A cash buyer has no lender to wait on, so the calendar is yours to set. A listing draws more bidders but adds showings, an inspection window and a loan approval.

The city is compact and mostly built out. Its estimated 46,236 residents in July 2025 share about 4.84 square miles, and just 52.2 percent of homes are owner occupied, so buyers include families, investors and people who plan to rent the place out.

  • Cash offer: no lender appraisal, a closing day you can often pick, usually as is.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, plus repairs, showings and a longer wait.
  • Owner sale: no commission, but contracts and disclosures are yours to run.

sections.h2: What is North Miami Beach like for a home seller?
sections.html:
North Miami Beach is an older, fully built suburb in northeast Miami-Dade County, laid out on a deliberate street plan with wide avenues. The city's own history page explains that its founder planned a "perfect city" in 1917 with 80 foot residential streets and 100 to 125 foot business thoroughfares, and that today's grid still follows that plan. Two of the original avenues are now Northeast 172nd Street and Northeast 19th Avenue.

The place began as the farming community of Ojus and the townsite of Fulford. Rock mining in the early 1900s left behind lakes, including Maule Lake and the lakes in the Sky Lake neighborhood, so some homes sit beside water that was once a quarry. The city incorporated as Fulford in 1927 after the 1926 hurricane, and a new charter in 1931 changed the name to North Miami Beach. A 1958 charter set up the council and manager form of government that the city still uses.

Landmarks buyers recognize include Greynolds Park, which opened as a county park in 1936 on an abandoned quarry site, and the Ancient Spanish Monastery on West Dixie Highway. State Road 826, also called North Miami Beach Boulevard, opened in 1951, and the 163rd Street shopping center followed in 1956. Residents commute along these corridors, and the average commute is 30.1 minutes.

sections.h2: What do North Miami Beach homes look like in Census data?
sections.html:
The Census figures point to moderate values, a big renter share and crowded households. Each row is a survey estimate for the whole city, not an appraisal of one property.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale cost in North Miami Beach?
sections.html:
The biggest state charge on a deed is documentary stamp tax, and Miami-Dade County is the one county with a different schedule from the rest of Florida. Read the department's documentary stamp tax page for the Miami-Dade wording, including how a single-family transfer is treated, and ask your title agent to run the number for your deed.

Who pays is a matter for the contract, even though the state looks to every party on the deed. Settle that line before you accept an offer. The clerk adds recording charges, which section 28.24 of the statutes spells out page by page.

  • Deed stamp tax: calculated by the title company on the sale price.
  • Recording charges: collected by the clerk when the deed is filed.
  • Mortgage, lien or delinquent tax payoffs: deducted from your proceeds.
  • Current year property tax: split between you and the buyer by closing date.

sections.h2: How does the county tax bill figure into my North Miami Beach sale?
sections.html:
The county appraiser fixes the value each January 1, and bills go out in November with a sliding early-payment discount. A sale ends your homestead exemption, and the new owner has to apply on his or her own by March 1. The appraiser's homestead page also warns owners about back taxes of up to ten years, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent annual interest when a change goes unreported, and it names renting the property as a risk.

Save Our Homes holds down the yearly rise in a homestead's assessed value, but a transfer of title resets the property to just value the next January 1. That is why a buyer's first full bill can come in well above yours. The Department of Revenue explains the mechanics in its Save Our Homes guide.

sections.h2: What if the house needs repairs or has code problems?
sections.html:
A house can be sold with open repairs, but permits and violations stay attached to the address, so learn what is open before you list. North Miami Beach runs permits, inspections and code violations through its eDMS online portal, where you can search records, check violations and request inspections.

Unpermitted work is the usual surprise. A porch enclosure, converted garage or added bathroom can stall a financed sale because the appraiser and insurer ask about it. Cash buyers often accept that risk, then lower the offer to cover it.

  • Look up the address in the portal for open permits and violations.
  • Collect receipts for the roof, windows, electrical and plumbing.
  • Order a lien search before you sign a contract.
  • Keep lease dates handy if a tenant lives there.

sections.h2: What if the house is a rental or an inheritance?
sections.html:
A rented house can be sold with the tenant in place, and an inherited one can be sold once someone has authority to convey it. Either way, the buyer wants proof of who may sign, so pull together the lease, the death certificate or the court papers early.

Short-term rentals add a local layer. The city's published application list includes a short-term rental registration for owners who list on platforms such as Airbnb or VRBO. Ask the city for the current rules before you advertise, because a buyer who plans to keep that use will ask whether the registration transfers.

Quitclaim deeds and contracts for deed are on the state's list of taxable documents, so handing a house to a relative before a sale is not automatically free of tax.

sections.h2: What steps lead from offer to closing?
sections.html:
Most of the waiting happens inside the title company's work, so the order of steps matters more than speed on your end.

  • Collect the deed, mortgage payoff, association contact and latest tax bill.
  • Weigh a cash offer, a listing price and your net after costs.
  • Sign a contract that names who pays stamp tax and which repairs you will do.
  • Wait for the title company to clear liens, open permits and unpaid taxes.
  • Sign the deed before witnesses or a notary and hand over keys.
  • The clerk records the deed and collects the tax.

Condominium and association properties add an estoppel letter and sometimes board approval, so request those early.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a North Miami Beach home sale?
faqs.a: The sales contract decides who pays, though the state holds every party to the deed liable. Miami-Dade has its own schedule, so have the title company calculate the exact figure for your deed.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The buyer files a new application with the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1, and the sale resets the assessed value the following January 1.

faqs.q: Is a sale possible with open permits at the house?
faqs.a: Yes, but the buyer will see them in a title or permit search. Expect a lower cash offer or a request to close the permit first. Search the address in the city's eDMS portal before you list.

faqs.q: How do I compare a cash offer with a listing?
faqs.a: Compare estimated net proceeds on each route, after commission, repairs and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house that is currently rented?
faqs.a: Yes. The tenant's lease generally continues, so give the buyer the lease terms early. Some cash buyers accept the tenant and others want the unit vacant at closing.
